root_idea.summary: The root centers on sustaining, preserving, and having power or control over something. Its clearest concrete expression is food that sustains bodily life; its extended applications include provision, preservation, guardianship, and capacity.
root_idea.development: The semantic field develops from holding and maintaining life through food and sustenance, and extends to supplying what sustains, preserving or guarding, and possessing power over a thing.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form قُوت; the Quranic form is its plural أَقْوَات.
Displayed as the active-participial citation form مُقِيت.

senses.definition: Food, sustenance, or provisions that sustain life.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural أَقْوَات refers to sustenance or provisions apportioned for the earth and its occupants.

senses.definition: One who gives food, nourishment, or sustenance; a sustainer.
senses.usage_conditions: In divine description, it denotes one who supplies each being with what sustains it.

senses.definition: A preserver, protector, watcher, or witness over a thing.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic divine description, the word is interpreted as one who preserves and watches over everything, and bears witness to it.

senses.definition: One possessing power or ability over a thing.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتًا, it is also interpreted as possessing power over everything.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed, nourish, or sustain someone by providing food sufficient to maintain life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer to supplying a person, household, family, or dependants with their needed provision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stint or restrict a household’s provision.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage associated with parsimony or poverty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To measure or portion food; alternatively, to make small round cakes from grain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as variant interpretations of the expression قُوتُوا طَعَامَكُمْ; the wording is construction-specific and the interpretations are not presented as universal senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To provide someone with what sustains him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction meaning to make available the food or provision on which someone subsists.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep, preserve, guard, or protect someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive preservation or protection use distinct from supplying food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have power or ability to do, accomplish, attain, or compass a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Takes عَلَى with the object of the action or achievement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To nourish oneself or subsist on something; to make something one’s food and eat it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe subsisting on only a small amount or on a specified thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be fed, nourished, or sustained; to feed oneself or eat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may occur with بِـ or without it, including the construction يَقْتَاتُونَ الحَبَّ, “they eat grain.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To consume or take away something little by little.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage describing gradual, piecemeal removal or consumption.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For war to consume or take camels as provision.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression in which camels are taken as payment of bloodwits.
An idiomatic figurative use, equivalent to speaking little.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a fire with fuel or other aliment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an idiom for supplying a fire with fuel, including feeding it gently and little by little.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone for food or provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X request construction taking قُوت as the thing requested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A qat tree, Catha edulis; also a species of lettuce known by a compound name containing قَات.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The botanical uses refer to named plants rather than the sustenance noun قُوت.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who feeds; substantivized, what is sufficient of the means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle may describe a feeder or, in the expression القَائِتُ مِنَ العَيْشِ, sufficient livelihood.
An established epithet, not a general restriction on the ordinary active-participle meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Acquainted with or knowledgeable about a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Arabic usage distinct from the Quranic divine descriptions of sustenance, preservation, and power.

cautions: مُقِيت in Quran 4:85 has several lexically attested interpretive readings—sustainer, preserver or witness, and possessor of power—which are kept as distinct but related senses.
The reported expression قُوتُوا طَعَامَكُمْ has variant traditional interpretations and is therefore presented as a construction-specific classical usage rather than a general definition of the root.
